subject: Autoscale SLO qualification - follow up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastpay.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-23T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Autoscale SLO qualification - follow up

Alex / Samir, thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical sync.

Recap (what we heard on the call):
- Latency targets: p50 ~ 120-150 ms, p95 <= 500 ms for typical 512-token prompts.
- Throughput: steady-state ~200 req/s, expected spikes up to 2x (400 req/s) for ~3-6 minutes.
- Concurrency: target concurrent sessions ~50.
- Streaming: token-level streaming required for our conversational UI (low per-token latency).
- Autoscale/burst: customer needs fast scale-up for marketing-driven bursts; ideally scale to peak within 90s, with a warm pool to reduce cold-start impact.

Questions / clarifications we need from you:
1) Can you confirm the 3-6 minute spike window and whether spikes are predictable (scheduled promos) vs fully ad-hoc?
2) Any hard SLA requirements for p99 or is p95 the main guarantee?
3) Are there other regions besides US traffic we should plan for?

What we propose (next steps):
- Attached: SLO_requirements_v1.pdf - initial SLO/scale behavior doc for review.
- Technical sync w/ infra + platform: propose Tue 2026-05-26 10:00 PT (30-45m). Please confirm availability.
- In parallel, please send a representative traffic trace/CSV (samples are fine) so Aditya can model warm pool sizing.

Quick note on autoscale behavior we recommend for FastPay (initial):
- Warm pool: maintain 4 pre-warmed nodes for low-latency baseline (can be adjusted after traffic analysis).
- Burst capacity: allow a 2x burst multiplier for up to 5 minutes with accelerated scale-up.
- Scale-up: aim for 90s to reach peak; background node spin-up continues to full capacity over 5 minutes.
- Queueing: short request queueing (<= 50 requests) with prioritized streaming responses; queueing should be accounted for in SLOs.

Please review and reply with confirmations/edits and attach the traffic file when you can.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attach: SLO_requirements_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@fastpay.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Autoscale SLO qualification - follow up

Thanks Marissa, good recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Spikes: about 60% of spikes are scheduled (promos), 40% are ad-hoc (user-driven). Scheduled spikes are fairly predictable (we can share a cadence).
2) p99: for checkout flows we care about tail latency, ideally p99 <= 1.2s, but p95 <= 500ms is most important for the general UX.
3) Regions: primarily US, small EU footprint (10%).

Regarding warm pool and scale-up: If the warm pool is exhausted, what's the expected additional latency distribution during the 90s? Do you offer any SLA credits or mitigations for tail events during scale-up?

I attached a sample traffic pattern (fastpay_traffic.csv). Could Aditya take a look and give recommended warm-pool sizing and any suggestions to reduce cold-start exposure?

Also we'd like to see a quick POC with streaming enabled - token-level granularity is critical for our UI.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | FastPay
alex.johnson@fastpay.com
Attach: fastpay_traffic.csv (text/csv)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-24T12:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Autoscale SLO qualification - follow up (internal)

Marissa / Neha, I reviewed Alex's traffic CSV and sketched out a few options. High-level notes:

- Warm-pool sizing: with the provided samples, a warm pool of 4 nodes covers ~1.6x baseline and absorbs the first minute of most scheduled bursts. For 2x spikes lasting 3-6 minutes, we recommend a warm pool of 6 nodes to keep p95 under 500ms for most cases.
- Scale-up profile:
  * Fast path: maintain a minimal warm pool + accelerated provisioning that brings additional nodes online within ~90s (best effort). During the first 90s, expect increased queuing for requests that exceed warm capacity; our models predict median added latency of ~80-200ms, p95 additions up to ~700ms depending on request size.
  * Full provisioning: reaches steady-state capacity by ~4-6 minutes for larger cluster sizes.
- Queueing behavior: we propose a short in-memory queue with configurable depth (default 50). Queued requests are prioritized for streaming where possible. We can expose queue depth and drop/overflow metrics to FastPay for alerting.
- Cold-start mitigations:
  * Warm pool + pre-warm on scheduled promos via webhook (FastPay can notify us ~2-5 mins prior) - reduces scale-up to ~30s in many cases.
  * Lightweight standby containers that can accept TCP connections immediately (lower throughput until fully ready).
- SLA credits: we'll need commercial sign-off, but we can propose an SLA carve-out that accounts for predictable scale-up windows and offer service credit language tied to restart/scale events.

Next steps I recommend from technical side:
- Confirm whether FastPay can provide a webhook 2-5 mins prior to scheduled promos.
- Run a 1-hour POC with streaming enabled against a shadow production workload to validate p95/p99 numbers.
- Schedule the joint tech sync proposed by Marissa - I can join and present the provisioning model.

I can turn these notes into a short technical note for Alex with recommended warm-pool sizing and a simulation graph if helpful.

Aditya
Staff Engineer, Platform Performance | Redwood Inference
